edits.headline: Saudi Arabia shuts East-West oil pipeline after drone attack from Iraq
edits.subheadline: The Saudi foreign ministry said drones from Iraq hit the pipeline in the Riyadh and Medina areas, causing injuries and damage.
editorialBody: Saudi Arabia temporarily shut its East-West oil pipeline as a precaution after drones launched from Iraq hit it, an Energy Ministry official said, Al Jazeera reported on 11 September.

The Saudi Foreign Ministry said it would not retaliate for now, at Baghdad's request. Iraq's prime minister's office said the drones were launched from Maysan province and dismissed the commander of operations there.

US President Donald Trump told Fox News he did not regret the war with Iran, Business Today reported on 11 September. "I don't believe in the word 'regret'," he said. He said he believed the war would end right after the November midterm elections.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian urged BRICS members to expand trade in national currencies at the BRICS Business Forum in New Delhi on 11 September, The Pioneer reported.
The death toll from a fire on the ferry M/V June Aster off Coron in Palawan, the Philippines, rose to 35, with 54 people missing, Al Jazeera reported on 11 September.
Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said investigators had obtained the names of other potential recruiters for Jeffrey Epstein, AFP reported on 10 September.
Inside Climate News reported that Winston County, Alabama, has arrested residents over unpaid trash bills. One of them, Pam Benton, 59, sat handcuffed to a bench inside the Winston County Courthouse.
